subject: Biology

stem: A cheek cell is 52 mm long in a printed micrograph. Its actual length is 65 micrometres.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Name the microscope accessory used to measure cell dimensions after calibration.

parts.label: b
parts.html: (i) Calculate the actual length if an image 34 mm long is shown at x800 magnification.

parts.label: b
parts.html: (ii) Calculate the magnification of the 52 mm cheek-cell image.

parts.label: c
parts.html: State two structures expected in both a cheek cell and a yeast cell.

questions.title: Microscopy and cell size

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Any two of plasma membrane, cytoplasm, nucleus, mitochondria, ribosomes.

stem: Leaves were sampled at four altitudes. Mean stomatal density and carbon isotope ratio are shown.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Name a suitable sampling method along the altitude gradient.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Compare stomatal density and isotope ratio across the gradient.

parts.label: c
parts.html: State one abiotic variable that should be measured.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Explain how guard cells regulate gas exchange.

questions.title: Altitude transect and leaf gas exchange

solparts.label: a
solparts.html: Transect with quadrats/sampling points at defined intervals.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Stomatal density generally increases with altitude while the isotope ratio becomes less negative; both change most strongly above 1400 m.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Temperature, light intensity, humidity, wind speed, soil moisture or carbon dioxide concentration.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Ion uptake lowers guard-cell water potential, water enters by osmosis and the pore opens; ion loss reverses this and closes the pore, controlling CO2 entry and water loss.

stem: Oxygen consumption by two jellyfish species was measured after acclimation at three temperatures.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Name a device suitable for measuring dissolved oxygen.

parts.label: b
parts.html: State one variable, other than temperature, that should be controlled.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Calculate the change in respiration rate for species A between 12 and 24 degrees C.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Compare the temperature responses of the two species.

parts.label: e
parts.html: Explain why oxygen uptake across a cell membrane does not require ATP.

questions.title: Temperature and jellyfish respiration

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Body mass, salinity, oxygen concentration, acclimation time or volume of water.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: Both increase from 12 to 18 degrees C; A continues to increase strongly at 24 degrees C, while B changes little from 18 to 24 degrees C.

solparts.label: e
solparts.html: Oxygen is small and non-polar; it moves down its concentration gradient through the phospholipid bilayer by simple diffusion.

stem: Root-tip cells were scored by mitotic stage, and adult heights were recorded in a separate population survey.

parts.label: a
parts.html: Identify the stage in which chromosomes first become visibly condensed.

parts.label: b
parts.html: Outline cytokinesis in an animal cell.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Estimate the modal height interval from the table.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Explain why ABO blood group is discrete variation whereas height is continuous variation.

questions.title: Cell division and human variation

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: The plasma membrane is pulled inward by a contractile ring; the cytoplasm divides to form two daughter cells.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html: ABO groups form distinct categories determined by multiple alleles/codominance with little environmental effect; height is polygenic and influenced by environment, producing a continuous range.
